name: SNO+ detector

technology.value: The original SNO 12 m acrylic vessel and PMT support structure, refilled first with ultrapure water, then with liquid scintillator, and eventually planned to be loaded with tellurium for a double-beta-decay search
technology.note: Structural continuity with the SNO vessel is per the official site's own description of SNO+ as reusing SNO's infrastructure; the specific scintillator mass figure is Wikipedia-sourced only.

placements.quote: The detector underwent a water-filled commissioning phase from 2017 to 2019
placements.note: Placed at site:snolab-underground-lab (owned by the facilities workstream; not created here), the same cavern as experiment:sno.

intervals.label: water-fill commissioning
intervals.quote: The detector underwent a water-filled commissioning phase from 2017 to 2019

intervals.label: liquid-scintillator phase
intervals.quote: In 2022, the detector was filled with Linear alkylbenzene (LAB) liquid scintillator loaded with the wavelength shifter PPO

target_mass.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only this session.

notes: Modelled as a distinct detector record from detector:sno despite sharing the same physical acrylic vessel/cavern, because the target medium and physics program changed materially (heavy water -> water -> liquid scintillator, eventually tellurium-loaded); see experiment:sno-plus.lineage (`upgrade_of` experiment:sno).

summary.plain: The same 12-metre acrylic ball that once held SNO's heavy water, now filled with liquid scintillator, watching for solar neutrinos, reactor antineutrinos, and a hoped-for rare nuclear decay.
summary.technical: SNO's original acrylic vessel and PMT support structure, water-filled 2017-2019 for commissioning, then filled with 780 t of LAB+PPO liquid scintillator from 2022; a future phase will load natural tellurium for a 0νββ search.
